pointers.sentence: A production WSGI server imports the project's `wsgi.py`, which calls `get_wsgi_application`: the settings are loaded, every installed application is imported and its models are registered in the app registry, and the handler is made, which builds the middleware chain from `settings.MIDDLEWARE` (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`).

The server calls `WSGIHandler.__call__`, which sends the `request_started` signal, wraps the server's dictionary in a `WSGIRequest` that parses the query string, the cookies and the body only when they are read, and calls the chain (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).

The route converts `2026` to an `int`; the CSRF middleware, offered the view before it is called, lets a `"GET"` through; and the view is called with `year=2026` (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`): [The URL is resolved and the view is called](overview/view.md).

The query runs when the template's loop asks how many rows there are: the `Query` is compiled to one `"SELECT"` by a `SQLCompiler`, a connection is opened, and each row becomes an instance of the model (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.execute_sql`, `django/db/models/base.py:Model.from_db`): [A queryset becomes SQL](overview/query.md).

Rendering runs the context processors and then each node, escaping each value in the loop as its `VariableNode` renders it, and `render` makes an `HttpResponse` of the string (`django/shortcuts.py:render`): [The template is rendered](overview/template.md).

When the server has sent the body it closes the response, which sends `request_finished`, and a receiver of that closes the database connection: with the default settings a connection lives for one request (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.close`, `django/db/__init__.py:close_old_connections`): [The response returns to the server](overview/response.md).
